label: The statistical disproportion in institutional attention (UN resolutions) combined with cognitive science on monocausal attribution establishes that anti-Zionist discourse exhibits the structural signature of a monocausal attribution pattern.

defeaters.description: Israel receives disproportionate attention not because of attribution bias but because of its unique geopolitical position: the largest recipient of US foreign aid, a nuclear-armed state occupying territory of another people, and a conflict with religious significance to billions. The disproportion in attention may be rationally justified by the disproportion in geopolitical leverage, not cognitive bias.

label: The best explanation for why mutually incompatible ideological movements converge on anti-Zionism -- despite sharing no positive program -- is that anti-Zionism functions as a shared attribution target rather than a coherent political ideology.

If a causal framework is analytically sound, it should predict or explain major regional events. Anti-Zionist frameworks failed to predict the Arab Spring and cannot explain major conflicts orthogonal to Israel. Therefore, anti-Zionist causal models produce systematic predictive failures.

Given that anti-Zionism persists despite demonstrated predictive failure, the best explanation is that it provides psychological-functional benefits (cognitive closure, coalitional solidarity) independent of analytical accuracy -- as predicted by the attribution-engine model from social psychology.

A framework that exhibits monocausal attribution and is sustained by psychological closure rather than accuracy will resist falsification -- counter-evidence is absorbed into the attribution schema rather than prompting revision.

Anti-Zionism is best explained as a causal attribution engine rather than a coherent political position because it (1) exhibits monocausal reasoning, (2) lacks ideological coherence, (3) produces systematic predictive failures, (4) persists through psychological rather than analytical mechanisms, and (5) resists falsification.

defeaters.description: Anti-Zionism may be a legitimate political critique of ethnonationalism applied specifically to the Israeli case, analogous to anti-apartheid movements. The fact that diverse groups oppose a specific state project does not make their position incoherent or attributional -- diverse groups also opposed apartheid South Africa without sharing a positive program. The thesis may confuse political opposition with cognitive bias.
